info.title: Ultiorganizer API
info.description: Read-only API for events, divisions, teams, games, gameplay, and version metadata, plus the endpoints a third-party scorekeeping app uses with a scorekeeping link.

ApiTokenAuth.description: Send the token as Authorization: Bearer <token>.

ScorekeepingLinkAuth.name: X-Scorekeeping-Token
ScorekeepingLinkAuth.description: The 32 hex characters of the scorekeeping link QR code (the t parameter of BASEURL/scorekeeper/?t=...). Never sent in the URL or the body.

number.description: Jersey number; null keeps an unnumbered player unnumbered.

time.description: Seconds into the game, not earlier than the previous goal. Must be null when the event hides goal times (rules.hide_time_on_scoresheet); the server then numbers the times.

GameData.description: The complete scoresheet content of one game. Every field is required and unknown fields are refused with 400 and their path. Empty lists clear. A null result requires no goals; a result with goals must equal the goal total.

home_team_id.description: Must match the fixture, else 409 fixture_changed.

time.description: Seconds into the game, not earlier than the last stored goal. Must be null when the event hides goal times; the server then uses the last goal's time plus one second.

team_id.description: The side's team in the fixture; another team is 409 fixture_changed.

Metadata.description: Only the fields sent are changed.

FinalScore.description: The score the app has been keeping. The stored score must be exactly this, else 409 score_changed.

WriteResult.description: Every live write answers with the game id, the resulting token (also the ETag), the result after the write and the operation's own fields.

get.summary: Everything the scorekeeping app needs to keep one game
get.description: One consistent read, taking no lock: game, both teams' eligible players and game rosters, goals, timeouts, spirit stoppages, result, starting offence, halftime, official, the rules, the state an upload keeps (cap events, forfeit, defences) and the concurrency token, also sent as the strong ETag. It contains no game notes, contact data or history. Goals carry num, home_score and away_score, which are derived by the server and must not be sent in an upload.

put.summary: Replace the whole scoresheet of a game
put.description: Replaces rosters, goals, timeouts, spirit stoppages, starting offence, halftime, official and the result in one transaction under the game lock. Game notes, cap events, defences and the clock of an ongoing game are kept. A forced scoresheet history snapshot is taken first, so the previous state can be restored from the desktop scoresheet history. If-Match carries the token from the entry context (or from the previous upload response); a mismatch is 409 stale_token and the app must fetch the entry context again. The same Idempotency-Key with the same body replays the stored answer without writing (Idempotent-Replay: true); with a different body it is 409 idempotency_conflict. A game going from final back to ongoing has its pool standings recomputed.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The token, quoted or bare. Missing is 428 precondition_required; * never matches.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Client-chosen key, 1 to 64 printable ASCII characters.

post.description: Appends one goal as the Scorekeeper goal form does. The server assigns num (last + 1) and the cumulative score, and raises the result to the new score unless a team's stored score is already higher. Scorer and assist must be on the side's game roster. Refused on a final game (409 game_final). A browser append taking the same num at the same moment is retried once, then 409 goal_changed. No If-Match: like the browser Scorekeeper, appends do not check the token.

post.description: For result-only keeping: adds one point to, or takes one from, a team's stored score in a single statement, as the Scorekeeper result page's taps do. The game becomes ongoing; back at 0-0 before the clock starts, it returns to not started. Refused on a final game (409 game_final) and outside 0 to 1000 (409 score_out_of_range).

post.description: Saves the score as the final result, resets the game clock and recomputes the pool standings and playoff moves in the same transaction. The stored score must still be the one sent (409 score_changed), so a point another device recorded since is not finalized over; a game with no score yet cannot be finalized this way. A different final score goes through score taps or the complete upload.
